channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers" - Have you joined the site because you want to write an SCP article or tale of your own, sometime now or in the future? Post your introduction here!

item.content:encoded:
Hi everybody!

I've been a fan of the SCP wiki since I saw it referenced on Tv tropes and finally worked up the nerve to create an account. I am constantly amazed by the new and creative ideas that are brought to the table by members of the community and am looking forwards to contributing my own.

item.content:encoded:

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello hello Sibilance! Welcome to the Wiki! I'm Ralliston, a site author and a member of the Community Outreach Team - with this helpful little comment, I'll try to help you find your way around the site and link a bunch of useful places and links that will help you in your SCP journey.

It's nice to see people who have been interested in the SCP Universe for a long time finally join our ~official~ place on the internet and make their way onsite. After all, here, you can affect the quality of works by voting and contributing yourself! It's very awesome to see that you are quite an open-minded person, willing to take all criticism into consideration - it's one of the best traits any artist can have!

Without further ado though, let's click the collapsible, shall we? :)

+ show block
– hide block

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our Sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts, which are in-works articles. Using it, you can link the drafts to reviewers to get their opinions on them before posting. It really helps everyone out a lot.

For brainstorming concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by experienced members of the community if you need help refining and fleshing out your concept. It's a very helpful little place for when you want to start your writing journey, especially when you're not sure if the idea is all that great.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles. Within the Guides, you will find useful information written by experienced members of the site for the use of newer ones.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success! Remember - there is no rush to writing - take your time! The more time you spend on fleshing your ideas out, the more your chance of success becomes!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community to implement into your very own writing. Alternatively, you might want to look at the User Curated Lists page, where members of the community list and rank their favorite articles in different genres and themes, showing which attempts at such are successful and what the community likes.

Best of luck with your future contributions to the site! I hope you enjoy your time here as much as we do! If you have any more questions, feel free to message me here on Wikidot or on the IRC chats!

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hi everybody,

I've been a kind of background fan of the Foundation since high school and have always liked the clinical format and style of writing. I'm hoping to write a few SCP articles and explore some interesting ideas through them, think less 'oh god the universe is collapsing!' and more 'it's weird that this exists'.

I'm hoping to sharpen my writing skills here and get some good feedback from the folks with experience (criticism is not only accepted but welcomed). My own experience in writing has mostly been short fiction and personal projects so this seems like the place to be to develop that.

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello everyone. I recently joined this site thanks to my roommate who used SCP-001, or one of them, as a setting for a D&D game. Since then I've been reading every single SCP I can in my free time and have been gathering my ideas. I decided it was finally time to join so I can start getting to know the writing process and the formatting for the articles. As far as my hobbies go I like sports, videogames and D&D. I also spend my free time imagining things, machines, places, or events so I hope to put that talent to good use here.

Thank you all for having me here. hope to talk to all of you soon.

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello everyone! I found out about this place years ago, maybe from a YouTube video? It was a long time ago so I can't remember exactly; it might've been The Volgun. Only a month ago did I finally take the jump and make an account. Anyway, I already have one main list article on the site (that I'm not happy with to be honest, I'll rewrite it one day). Even so, it survived I guess? Not bad for what was basically a coldpost! Anyway, I thought I'd make the effort to formally introduce myself! I'm new to writing fiction, but I have experience in scientific writing (academic papers and whatnot), so I'm hoping to bring these skills to to table in my future articles. The biggest problem I have is actually coming up with decent ideas.

I currently have an idea on the Idea Critique Forum I'm hoping to have looked at before I take it to the draft stage.

So yeah, that's me. I hope I'll contribute something worth reading some day!

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hi!

I've known about this site for a long time, since middle school actually! After seven years of lurking in the shadows, I finally decided to join! I want to at least try to write a couple SCPs or anomalous items if a particularly nice idea hits and sticks.

I love to draw and think about the relatively impossible alongside things concerning cosmology/astrophysics and psychology.

The one thing I'm a bit worried about is grabbing a Sandbox page and using it correctly, but other than that I've wandered around the site a couple times.

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Right. Greetings all!

I found out about SCP… well, gosh, a few years ago. I found an image of a rather cute orange pile of slime, and a few sites later, I had found the scp wiki. Once I read the article, I clicked 998… then 997… and I was hooked.

I'd love to contribute to the site in the form of some scips. In terms of authors that I especially like, Dr. Gears, Kain, and Clef have to be some of my favorites.

It's a real honour to be here!

item.content:encoded: Hello everyone. Turns out that spontaneously applying to the SCP wiki and writing an article starts to seem like a completely reasonable use of time after working on a term project for long enough. item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello! After years of being too lazy to join, I finally made an account. Believe it or not, I've actually been a fan of the SCP Wiki since elementary school, probably around fourth grade? I was introduced to it by my sister, who just really liked giving me nightmares. I was instantly hooked though; I have vivid memories of browsing random articles on the school laptops when I probably wasn't supposed to. I've been in love with horror and weird fiction since, and it's honestly a huge influence on who I am today.

Though I've been a fan for awhile now, I recently rediscovered how much I love this website. For the past few days I've been doing NOTHING but reading SCP articles, drawing fanart, writing fanfic, and resisting the urge to annoy my friends by rambling about it. Now I'm really interested in writing my own SCP, and though I'm super nervous, I'm having a ton of fun coming up with ideas.

I'm constantly amazed by the sheer amount of creativity and talent in this community, and I'm thrilled to eventually contribute to it myself. =)

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello everyone,
I've been interested in SCP related media for about a decade now, it has always seemed really interesting and fun to me. I love thinking of weird things, and coming up with newer, weirder things! I plan on making many new posts, and I look forward to contributing to this awesome community.

Something that keeps me up at night is thinking about how every moment of my life that's in the past seems to have gone by in an instant, but everything that hasn't happened feels like it's so far away. When I'm on my deathbed someday, will I look back at my life as being instantaneous?

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded: Hello everybody! I joined this site because I have always been interested in the foundation and want to someday write an scp of my own! I greatly enjoy the "purely scientific" format all entries are written in. Objects that do not fall under normal scientific law, including supernatural phenomenon are some of my favorite things to explore and I am excited to be able to create my own.

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
How do you do. I'm Piecemaker and I am honored to at last find myself in the Foundation.

I've been reading through various documentation for years with many favorites to speak of, and have recently decided it might be time for me to write one of my own. I'm gathered numerous experiences over the years through games, books, movies and I've always had a thing for creepy or unsettling things, which is why I often recommend SCP to my colleagues and friends.

That being said, I wish for my first document to be on a humanoid SCP. I have a rather specific concept in mind that I've been going over in my head for weeks. Now, I know, it's not recommended to start with a humanoid. How do I know? Because I've read through every guide I could get my hands on, from "So you wanna write a humanoid" to "Things what do a thing", as well as going through some 50 crits in the Ideas critique forum to see common pitfalls. I am nevertheless terrified of falling into an X-man syndrome or another common mistake, as the concept is rather close to me. Either way, I intend to give it my very best effort. See you in the Crit Forum.

Hello hello Doctor Merigold! Welcome to the Wiki! I'm Ralliston, a site author and a member of the Community Outreach Team - with this helpful little comment, I'll try to help you find your way around the site and link a bunch of useful places and links that will help you in your SCP journey. We're very happy to see more people interested in extending their artistic skills with some knowledge you might only find here, on the SCP WIki. I can totally understand why you got attracted to the SCP Universe through its mysteries and secret knowledge sprinkled throughout its numerous articles - hopefully, you'll have as much fun reading them as the community had putting them together!

Without further ado though, let's click the collapsible, shall we? :)

+ show block
– hide block

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our Sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts, which are in-works articles. Using it, you can link the drafts to reviewers to get their opinions on them before posting. It really helps everyone out a lot.

For brainstorming concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by experienced members of the community if you need help refining and fleshing out your concept. It's a very helpful little place for when you want to start your writing journey, especially when you're not sure if the idea is all that great.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles. Within the Guides, you will find useful information written by experienced members of the site for the use of newer ones.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success! Remember - there is no rush to writing - take your time! The more time you spend on fleshing your ideas out, the more your chance of success becomes!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community to implement into your very own writing. Alternatively, you might want to look at the User Curated Lists page, where members of the community list and rank their favorite articles in different genres and themes, showing which attempts at such are successful and what the community likes.

Best of luck with your future contributions to the site! I hope you enjoy your time here as much as we do! If you have any more questions, feel free to message me here on Wikidot or on the IRC chats!

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hi everyone!

I love creative stories and heard about the SCP a few months ago. After looking at the site and reading both old and new articles, I can see that this is something really special. In a way, the stories here give me the same sense of awe and wonder I get when reading about ancient Egyptian or Greek mythology, except with a special 21st-century internet twist. I have an idea or two for an SCP article, and it would be an honor to have it accepted someday (after many, many rounds of feedback and rewrites of course:))

One thing that keeps me up at night is probably the inner workings of how we communicate. Language is so complex, yet I sometimes find myself struggling to find how best to phrase an idea or viewpoint.

I'm very excited to be a part of this community, and I hope I'll get to know many of you as we add to this pantheon of the 21st century!

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello, I am an author interested in adding an SCP to the site sometime in the near future. I've known about the foundation for around 2-3 years but I've just recently (past 3-4 months) started to really get into it. I hope that sometime in the near future I can add an SCP that many can enjoy.

As for the random question, there are a couple things that keep me up at night. The most common are made up scenarios, often involving putting myself in a characters shoes from a book or show that I enjoy. Otherwise, its thoughts of the past and what could have been.

Hello, everybody. I guess call me Ainulindale (Ay-noo-LIN-duh-lay). I've been reading "The Silmarillion" and since character names are difficult to obtain as a user id, I went with the name of the first story. I just discovered SCP by accident and it was exactly what I needed to find but didn't know I was looking for.

While watching youtube videos about different gods/angels/esoteric writings (Nag Hammadi library, for example) and a video called something like "SCPs that could end the world" was in the suggestion list. When I googled SCP, I saw what it was and immediately became excited. I've been published, but I pretty much stopped a while ago. I feel that working to write for the SCP Foundation will help me hone my writing skills once more. I'm still familiarizing myself with the SCP universe but I will eventually contribute. I want to do it right though and will be looking to you all for guidance. Thanks for making and maintaining such a great project!

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded: Hey there guys, hope you're doing well. Guess I'll introduce myself. When I was younger I loved reading, but for some reason I dropped it along the way. The SCP foundation gave me the chance to rediscover my old passion (and the stuff here certainly is better than those old child books). I've been a long time reader (maybe 2 years?), and due to not-so-good circumstances in my life I thought it would be nice to test myself as a writer, develop new skills and overall improve as a person trough something I really enjoy. Aside from that, there's not much else to say. My life mostly consist of studying, listening to weird music and playing my guitar. Also, English is not my native language so please excuse me if what I write seems messy. I hope we can all coexist and contribute to the wiki in a positive way!

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hi everybody!

My name's Patrick, I suppose it'd be appropriate to link to my Twitter and Medium pages once I've qualified for an author's page, somehow I imagine that is gauche at this stage.

I'm 35, founder of a cryptocurrency derivatives layer protocol, active Bitcoin trader, former social games designer and indie game designer. Co-founded a blog about indie games called Play This Thing! with an older GD in '07. Wrote my first short story when I was 7 about a dragon that gets progressively bigger as it eats things until it achieves the scale of celestial bodies (which in retrospect is very SCP-ish). Wrote a novel when I was 17 which was basically a less-good highschool themed take on Rules of Attraction. Went to college for creative writing after dropping out of CS to focus on designing/producing videogames. Started and failed to complete a number of novels. Started writing sci-fi actively in 2012/13, then lapsed a few years focusing on my career in Bitcoin protocol extension, then stated actively again in 2019.

+ show block
– hide block

I've never been a big horror fan, except for zombies and other things with some balance and procedurality. Getting creeped out by some of the classic SCP articles (Reagan-cut-up ending still hits), probably the first time I was experiencing the genre the way most horror fans do. I'm attracted to the sci-fi and abstraction elements of the verse, the extreme ontological flexibility, and the campy surrealism of the media SCPs, which seems to be my niche.

I went in guns blazing yesterday with my first two scips and got nary an upvote, because, execution/details and tangents aside, I think riding the line between mundane, crappy modern world phenomena and anomalies has to be done with great precision to stay on-theme in the verse. It's ok, they were expendable. I'd rather get a comment from a physics PhD, describing the nuances of candling distant galaxies than an upvote, if I have to choose. Of 12 I've drafted in a manic (perhaps anomalous?) frenzy over the past week I think the best ones related to media and narratology/pataphysics so I'm engaging with the community to iterate on those. I have several ideas for canon/mythos extension and film adaptations, and I am *very* open to collaboration. I enjoy giving feedback on concepts and may volunteer for a flight onto the review crew in Q1 '21, if IRL commitments give me the time. I'd like to see some arc of development in the meta-mythos (plausibly deniable metaplot that spans multiple canons) and am super open to collaboration and constellation/collation about that.

I really like the idea of the wiki becoming this uber-House-of-Leaves hypertext construct that acts as a sort of mythology of hypermodernity. I like the idea of 6 series being hypermodernity themed and the eventual 7 series being transhumanism themed. I prefer a Chaos Insurgency that involves subversion and infiltration to the transhuman-reinforced-skeleton soldiers, rather, I think the dystopic trend in the Foundation going in that direction is very interesting.

I have experience running treasury/admin on an actual semi-esoteric foundation relating to building a cryptocurrency protocol (funded by the first ICO in 2013). In 2015 I called out the former director for basically embezzling 200k+, a year later I sort of got end-run by a fellow board member, the co-founder of Tether, and branched out on my own. So I have a lot of insights into Foundation governance and coups that I think, could combine with some other author's styles, and reinforce the meta-mythos and the Inside Baseball of Foundation life for Class 3-5 personnel.

My favorite SCP-001 proposal is Lily's "Beautiful Day". I think the verse could use more of that uncannily heavenly vibe.

Ok that's enough wall of text. I'm seasoned enough in writing not to make it all about my ego as an artist, iteration is the key, anyone please feel free to DM me links to concepts/drafts/headcanon ideas.

Cheers!


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn
